summary: Modern data platforms are embedding AI/ML directly into the database layer, letting teams run inference, generate embeddings, and perform semantic/vector search where the data already lives — minimizing data movement and simplifying governance. Capabilities range from SQL-callable LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML) to native vector indexes (MongoDB Atlas, Databricks Vector Search) and extension-based approaches (pgvector on PostgreSQL and Aurora). Vector-based retrieval is rapidly becoming standard, with Gartner projecting 30% of enterprises will rely on it for GenAI by 2026 and the vector database market expected to reach ~$17.9B by 2034.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI — managed LLM and ML functions callable via SQL/Python
databases.description: Cortex provides serverless access to LLMs (for completion, summarization, translation, sentiment, extraction) and task-specific ML functions, plus Cortex Search and embedding functions. Available within Snowflake and extended to Snowflake Postgres, allowing AI inference and embedding generation directly alongside operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type and native vector similarity functions, plus Cortex Search as a managed semantic/hybrid retrieval service. In Snowflake Postgres, vector storage and querying are supported natively alongside Cortex functions.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in via Cortex functions (e.g., COMPLETE, EMBED_TEXT, SUMMARIZE) supporting hosted models from providers like Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and Snowflake's own models — no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex LLM functions billed by tokens processed and compute credits. Vector/embedding operations and Cortex Search incur serverless compute charges on top of standard Snowflake warehouse/storage costs.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration — train, deploy, and run inference using SQL
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts build and run models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization) directly with SQL. It integrates tightly with Vertex AI to call hosted foundation models (Gemini) for generation, embeddings, and remote inference, and supports generating/storing embeddings in BigQuery.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides a VECTOR_SEARCH function and vector indexes for approximate nearest-neighbor search over stored embeddings, enabling semantic search natively within the warehouse.
databases.llm_integration: Native via remote models that connect to Vertex AI (Gemini family) and ML.GENERATE_TEXT / ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML priced by bytes processed or flat-rate/slot compute for training and queries; LLM/remote inference incurs additional Vertex AI model charges. Vector index storage and search consume standard query/compute pricing.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database AI model calls
databases.description: pgvector adds a vector column type and similarity operators to open-source PostgreSQL, making it a popular choice for RAG and semantic search. pgai (from Timescale) extends this by enabling embedding generation and LLM calls to providers like OpenAI directly from SQL, keeping embeddings and source data co-located.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided by the pgvector extension (with HNSW and IVFFlat indexes); it is first-party open source but still an extension rather than a built-in engine capability.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension and LangChain/application frameworks, which call external LLM/embedding APIs (OpenAI, Vertex AI, local models like Ollama) from SQL or application code.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs are the underlying Postgres hosting/compute plus any external LLM/embedding API usage fees. Managed offerings (Timescale, Supabase, etc.) add hosting charges.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-invoked inference via Amazon SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you call ML models from SQL by integrating Aurora (MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible) with SageMaker for custom models, Bedrock for foundation/LLM access, and Comprehend for NLP. This enables in-query predictions and generative outputs without building a separate serving pipeline.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively in Aurora ML itself. Vector similarity search on Aurora PostgreSQL relies on the pgvector extension; Aurora ML focuses on model inference, not a built-in vector engine. Mark as extension-based, not native.
databases.llm_integration: Integrated with Amazon Bedrock for foundation models (e.g., Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan) and SageMaker/Comprehend, callable from SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML integration itself; you pay standard Aurora compute/storage plus usage fees for the invoked SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend services.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — create and run models with SQL via Amazon SageMaker and Bedrock
databases.description: Redshift ML allows data warehouse users to create, train, and deploy models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, with SageMaker Autopilot handling model selection behind the scenes. It supports in-database predictions and integration with Bedrock foundation models for generative use cases on warehouse data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Redshift ML is focused on predictive model training/inference; it does not provide a built-in production vector-search index. Vector workloads typically use external stores or other AWS services.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for LLM/foundation-model inference and SageMaker for custom models, invoked through SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift ML uses existing Redshift compute for in-cluster models; training via SageMaker and LLM inference via Bedrock incur their respective service charges in addition to standard Redshift costs.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI for model training/serving/agents and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling — foundation model fine-tuning, model serving, agent frameworks, RAG, and evaluation — on the lakehouse. Databricks Vector Search is a managed, serverless vector database integrated with Unity Catalog for governance and automatic sync of embeddings from Delta tables.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in managed vector index that supports approximate nearest-neighbor search and automatically keeps embeddings in sync with source Delta tables.
databases.llm_integration: Native via Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs (hosted models plus ability to serve open and fine-tuned models), with built-in embedding model support.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based on Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search billed by compute/serving endpoints, and Model Serving / Foundation Model APIs billed by tokens or provisioned throughput plus cloud infrastructure costs.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector indexing and semantic search in the document database
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run semantic, hybrid, and RAG queries using MongoDB's aggregation pipeline. It is designed so vector data lives with application data, simplifying GenAI app development without a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas provides a built-in vector search index type ($vectorSearch) with approximate nearest-neighbor search integrated into the query/aggregation engine.
databases.llm_integration: No bundled LLM; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Vertex AI, Bedrock, Hugging Face) and frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex to generate embeddings and power RAG.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes or shared cluster resources, so cost scales with cluster tier/Search Node sizing plus any external embedding/LLM API usage.
